connect.title: Your vault
connect.lead: The address you open in your browser to use Family Document Vault.
connect.invalid: That doesn't look like an address. It's the one you open in your browser, such as vault.example.com.
connect.notAVault: That address answered, but it isn't a Family Document Vault. Check the address — it's the one you open in your browser.
connect.unreachable: Can't reach {{host}}. Is this phone on the same Wi-Fi as the vault, or connected to your VPN?
connect.setupRequired: This vault hasn't been set up yet. Finish setting it up in a browser on a computer, then come back.
connect.serverTooOld: Your vault is on version {{server}}. This app needs {{needed}} or newer. Whoever looks after the vault can update it — it usually takes a few minutes.
connect.clientTooOld: This version of the app is too old for your vault. It needs {{needed}} or newer; you have {{client}}. Update the app to carry on.
connect.apiVersion: This vault speaks a different version of the app's language ({{server}}). Update the app, or ask whoever looks after the vault.
connect.askHttp: {{host}} doesn't use a secure connection. On your own Wi-Fi that's usually fine; anywhere else, other people on the network could see what you send. Use it on this Wi-Fi?
connect.refusePublicHttp: The app only uses an unencrypted address inside your home network. Ask whoever runs the vault for its https:// address.
connect.refuseMobileData: This vault's address isn't secure, so the app only uses it on Wi-Fi.
connect.stranger: Something else is answering at {{host}} — not the vault you signed in to. Nothing was sent. If the vault was reinstalled, sign in again.
connect.reinstalled: This vault has been reinstalled since you last signed in. Sign in again.
connect.certificateUntrusted: This phone doesn't trust your vault's certificate yet. If your vault makes its own certificate, install it on this phone once — here's how.
connect.certificateWrongName: Your vault's certificate is for a different name. Use the address the certificate was made for — the one your browser shows when you open the vault.
connect.certificateExpired: Your vault's certificate has run out — or this phone's date is wrong. Check the date in the phone's settings; if it is right, whoever looks after the vault can renew the certificate.
connect.guideAndroid1: 1. Get the certificate file from whoever looks after your vault. For a vault that makes its own, it is vault-ca.crt (the vault's README says how to copy it out).
connect.guideAndroid2: 2. Put the file on this phone, then open Settings and search for "CA certificate" (it is under Security, then Encryption & credentials, then Install a certificate).
connect.guideAndroid3: 3. Android warns that a certificate you install can vouch for websites. Choose Install anyway, then pick vault-ca.crt.
connect.guideAndroid4: 4. Come back here and connect again.
connect.guideAndroidRemove: It stays until you remove it, under Encryption & credentials, then User credentials.
connect.guideIphone: Open vault-ca.crt on this iPhone and install the profile it offers (Settings, General, VPN & Device Management). Then turn on full trust for it in Settings, General, About, Certificate Trust Settings. Come back here and connect again.
connect.captivePortal: Something answered, but it looks like a Wi-Fi sign-in page. Finish signing in to the Wi-Fi, then try again.
connect.linkJoin: Invitations are accepted in the browser. Open it there, then come back and sign in.
connect.linkReset: Password resets are finished in the browser. Open it there, then come back and sign in.
connect.linkShared: That's a link for someone outside the family. It opens in the browser.

newNote.name: Title

unneeded.done: Marked as no longer needed. Its reminders have stopped.
unneeded.againDone: Needed again: its reminders are back as its dates say.

trashList.title: Trash
trashList.words: What was moved to the Trash, newest first. Restore puts it back where it was; removing anything for good is done in the browser.
trashList.needsConnection: The Trash needs a connection to the vault.

remind.title: Remind me
remind.badDay: Not a date: write it as {{example}}

share.title: Share outside the family
share.badDay: Not a day: write it as 14 Nov 2026
share.opensProblem: A number from 1 to 1000, or leave it empty for no limit.
share.noneInIt: Nothing in this collection can go on a link.
share.followWords: What is put in it later goes too. The link lasts {{days}} days at most.
share.onlyMeWarning: This document is Only me: whoever the link is for will see it.
share.onlyMeRefused: This household does not share Only me documents outside the family. An owner can change that in the browser.
share.secretApart: Send it another way than the link: a text if the link went by email.
share.onlyNow: The link is shown only now. Send it or copy it before you close this.

share.againLater: You can see this link, and its PIN or password, again in More → Sharing.

share.phoneProblem: That doesn’t look like a mobile number.
share.codeByText: When they open it, a code is texted to {{to}}.
share.emailMessageRules: Up to {{max}} characters and five lines. No web addresses or website names: the only link in the email is the vault’s.
share.emailNote: The vault emails the link, who it is from and when it stops working — never what it is to, and never its PIN or password. Tell them those another way.
share.emailBadAddress: That is not an email address. Check it: name@example.com.
share.emailSent_one: Sent to {{to}}. It can be emailed once more today.
share.emailSent_other: Sent to {{to}}. It can be emailed {{count}} more times today.
share.emailSentNoMore: Sent to {{to}}. That is as many times as it can be emailed today.
share.emailLimit: The vault has emailed this link as many times as it sends in a day. Copy it and send it yourself, or try again tomorrow.
share.emailUnavailable: This vault cannot email links just now. Copy the link and send it yourself.
share.linkPaused: That link is paused just now, so it would not open for them. Once it works again, you can email it.
share.linkEnded: That link no longer opens. Make a new one if you need to.
share.notRevealable: That link was made before the vault kept a copy of it. Send it yourself, or end it and make a new one.

sharing.none: Nothing is shared outside the family.

twoStep.offWords: Your password alone will sign you in. Type a code from your authenticator app to turn it off.
